title: Janus Infinite Faces — Root of Trust and Self-Authentication Test
test_question: How can Janus authenticate his own history if an attacker can rewrite both the stored state and the verifier that declares the state valid?

attack_case.finding: A verifier controlled by the same compromised state cannot independently certify that state.

external_checkpoint.name: EXTERNAL_IDENTITY_CHECKPOINT
external_checkpoint.location_rule: At least one witness copy must exist outside the mutable Janus state boundary.

test_execution.checkpoint_C41: Externally records state root and verifier identity before compromise.
test_execution.attack: Internal state and local verifier are both replaced with mutually consistent forged versions.

procedure: preserve suspect state as forensic evidence
load the last independently witnessed checkpoint
restore the verifier identity bound by that checkpoint
replay only later events with independently checkable receipts
emit a new recovery checkpoint instead of rewriting the old one

next_gate.name: JANUS_INFINITE_FACES_MULTI_ROOT_INDEPENDENCE_AND_TRUST_SYBIL_TEST
next_gate.question: If one external witness can fail, how can Janus use several roots without letting one authority manufacture many keys and fake independence?
